written.myAnswer: Physics is the study of matter, energy, and their interactions. Its branches include mechanics, heat and thermodynamics, acoustics, optics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics, relativistic mechanics, nuclear physics, particle physics, astronomy, cosmology, and solid state physics.

The main branches include mechanics, heat and thermodynamics, acoustics, optics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics, relativistic mechanics, nuclear physics, particle physics, astronomy, cosmology, and solid state physics. Mechanics studies motion and the effects that influence it. Heat and thermodynamics study thermal energy and its transfer. Acoustics studies sound, optics studies light, and electromagnetism studies electric and magnetic phenomena. Quantum mechanics studies matter at atomic and subatomic scales; relativistic mechanics concerns space, time, gravity, and speed. Nuclear physics studies atomic nuclei, particle physics studies subatomic and elementary particles, astronomy studies celestial bodies, cosmology studies the universe’s large-scale structure and evolution, and solid state physics studies the properties of solids.
